Nothing really interests me anymore—not books, not music, not even organizing the archives, which used to calm me. I just go through the motions. I forget things too—where I put files, appointments, even my keys. I tell myself it's just stress, but deep down, I wonder if I’m losing my mind.

There are times when I hear someone say something casual, like a comment on the weather, and I’m convinced they’re really talking about me—some kind of hidden message. I know it sounds odd, but it feels real in the moment. And sometimes, late at night, I feel something crawling on my arms, like insects, but when I look, there’s nothing there. I’ve checked the bedsheets, the windows—nothing. It stops when I focus on breathing, but it comes back.

I’ve had thoughts—dark ones. “I’d be better off dead,” that sort of thing. Not seriously, not with a plan, just… a quiet wish. I push through work because I have to, but some days, I don’t see the point. I can’t tell if the thoughts and sensations are from the sadness… or if the sadness is just following something else, something older.
D015-D005_h001.question_a:

I used to love the quiet precision of my job, but now I can’t even focus long enough to finish a single shelf. I keep misplacing things, forgetting where I just put a folder, and I know my supervisor’s starting to notice. It’s not just forgetfulness—I can’t concentrate at all, like my mind’s wrapped in fog.

I don’t enjoy anything, not even the old films I used to collect. Most days, I lie in bed thinking, “I just don’t want to be here.” I don’t have a plan, but the thought of being gone feels like relief.  

And then there are the other things—things I know sound crazy. Sometimes I feel like people’s conversations or random noises are sending me messages, like the radiator clanging is trying to tell me I’m worthless. I also feel things crawling on my skin—fingers tracing my arms when no one’s there. But these only started after the sadness took over. When I’m feeling slightly better, those sensations fade. They don’t happen on their own—only when the depression is bad.

I’ve been… gone, for about four months now. Just going through the motions at the shop, chopping and wrapping meat like a machine. My wife passed two years ago, but lately it feels like something heavier settled in. I can’t feel anything—no sadness, no anger, nothing. It’s like my soul’s been numbed. 

Lately, I keep seeing her—clear as day—in the back room of the butcher shop. She doesn’t speak, just watches. And not just her… sometimes figures in white coats standing near the freezers, though no one else sees them. I know it doesn’t make sense, but I’m sure I’ve done something terrible. I didn’t just lose her—I *killed* her. I must’ve. Why else would God make me survive and not her? I keep thinking about using the band saw. I’ve pictured it: after closing, when it’s just me and the lights overhead. I’d know how—it’s sharp, fast. No one would hear over the exhaust fan.

People say I’ve changed. I used to be proud of my cuts, but now I can’t focus. Orders get wrong. But part of me also thinks… maybe I’m meant for more. I’ve had moments—rare ones—where I feel like I’m not just a butcher. Like I have a message, something divine. But then the guilt comes crashing back. I don’t know what’s real anymore.
